note: Positions paraphrased neutrally from each party's own published materials (platforms, policy pages, campaign releases) as of 2026-10-05; 'news' entries report explicit party commitments. lean places a position on the issue's viewQuestion scale: -2 strongly poleA, +2 strongly poleB, 0 mixed, null if it does not map clearly. Absence of an issue means no clear position was found, not that the party has none. Campaign positions may change; most parties had not published full platforms.

bc-ndp.statusNote: No full 2026 platform published as of 2026-10-05; positions from 2026 campaign releases, the 'Action for You' page, and news reports.

positions.summary: Would temporarily cut the provincial fuel tax by 10 cents a litre and have regulators cap excess fuel industry margins.
Would triple its recruitment of U.S. health workers, adding loan forgiveness and relocation help, focused on cancer, emergency and rural care.
Would raise the speculation and vacancy tax, add a tax on condos left unsold over a year, and put revenue toward affordable homes.
Aims to double critical mineral exports, shorten mine approval timelines, expand Prince Rupert's port, and train a union-led mining workforce.
Would raise the top two income tax rates by two points and add a bracket over $1 million, funding health care and cost relief.
Says it is building involuntary care beds across the province and opening more youth mental health centres.
Supports continued LNG expansion, requiring new LNG projects to be net-zero-ready by 2030; aims to protect 30% of land by 2030.

conservative-party.statusNote: Platform page says 'coming soon' and lists topic headings only; positions from 2026 campaign releases and news reports.

positions.summary: Pledges no new or increased taxes and would remove PST on Canadian beer, wine and spirits.
Says it would lower the cost of building and buying homes by reducing taxes and red tape; opposes new housing taxes.
Would pass a 120-day permitting law for major projects and aim to double natural gas production by 2032.
Says it would grow the economy to reduce the deficit, without raising taxes; leader declined to set a date for balance.
States it would repeal the Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act (DRIPA).
Plans to cut red tape and speed project approvals to triple LNG production by 2035, with expanded First Nations ownership.

bc-green-party.statusNote: 'Our Plan' priorities published, full platform still 'coming soon' as of 2026-10-05; positions from Our Plan and 2026 campaign releases.

positions.summary: Would lift the freeze on $10-a-day child care spaces and reach universal free child care by 2031.
Would open community health centres in every region, complete nurse-to-patient ratios, and keep public health funding in public care.
Would restart community and Indigenous housing funds aiming for 26,000 units yearly, and tie rent limits to the unit.
Favours community-owned renewable energy and union jobs over new fossil fuel expansion, redirecting public support from LNG.
Would raise revenue from large corporations and very wealthy people, including a windfall tax, to fund housing and health care.
Would expand regulated supply, supervised consumption and voluntary treatment, decriminalize personal possession, and opposes involuntary care.
Would implement DRIPA through further legislation and co-develop a dispute-resolution mechanism with Indigenous peoples.
Would stop new fossil fuel development, fully fund old-growth logging deferrals, and update mining laws to protect communities.

centrebc.statusNote: No platform published; positions from party statements dated Nov 2025 to Aug 2026, before the current leader took over.

positions.summary: Would remove PST on food production and farm equipment and aims to make $10-a-day child care available to every family.
Would expand home care for seniors and reduce doctors' paperwork.
Proposed a three-part extortion plan: a joint financial-police-border unit, business security grants, and a dedicated prosecution team.
Does not commit to repealing DRIPA; favours one provincial reconciliation framework, sector agreements, and clear project timelines.
Supports pipelines only with conditions: Indigenous participation, an energy future fund, safety and climate safeguards, and local jobs.

onebc.statusNote: No formal platform document; positions from the party's 'Priorities' page.

positions.summary: Would cut every income tax bracket, including corporate, by 25% and reduce PST by two points.
Supports private health care alongside public care and shifting administrative spending to frontline staff.
Would eliminate the Step Code building requirements and block municipal rent control programs.
Would audit provincial regulations to cut them, reduce stumpage fees, and speed forestry permits.
Would balance the budget within four years, aim for surpluses, and use part of surpluses to repay debt.
Would focus justice resources on repeat and violent offenders and have prosecutors weigh past charges as danger indicators.
Would end safe supply and consumption sites, convert sites to recovery centres, and use involuntary rehab for severe addiction.
Would repeal DRIPA, halt voluntary transfers of land and resources to band governments, and restore oversight of band spending.
Would raise the annual allowable forest cut and approve an oil pipeline to Prince Rupert or Kitimat.

communist-party-of-bc.statusNote: Positions from the party's 'Our Platform' page (undated).

positions.summary: Would remove income tax on earnings under $50,000, cap rents at 20% of income, and double social assistance rates.
Would end private contracting in health care, add hospital beds, and provide universal pharmacare, dental and optical coverage.
Would build 100,000 social and low-income public housing units and ban renovictions and no-fault evictions.
Would raise minimum wage to $30, create union jobs through public investment, and retrain fossil fuel workers.
Would fund services through higher taxes on wealthy people and corporations and end LNG subsidies.
Would reduce police spending, increase civilian oversight of police, and remove police from schools.
Would decriminalize drugs, expand safer supply and harm reduction, and end involuntary care in favour of treatment on request.
Supports Land Back and Indigenous title, keeping DRIPA, and requiring Indigenous approval for resource extraction.
Would cut emissions, prioritize renewables, cancel LNG subsidies and the Ksi Lisims project, and protect old-growth forests.
Would raise per-student funding by $1,000, reduce class sizes, and hire more teachers and support staff.

christian-heritage-party-of-bc.statusNote: Positions from the party's 'Platform priorities' page.

positions.summary: Would reduce taxes, fees and regulatory costs, opposing raising costs and then returning money through programs.
Prioritizes timely care, home and palliative care, and shifting administrative spending to front-line care.
Would use suitable Crown land near communities for housing and fast-track approvals while cutting government-imposed building costs.
Would streamline permitting, support resource and trades sectors, and expand apprenticeships and training for B.C. residents.
Would review administrative and consulting spending, end failing programs, and restore fiscal discipline while protecting core services.
Would focus police and prosecutors on violent and repeat offenders and better coordinate with mental health and addiction services.
Makes recovery the goal: more detox and treatment, and involuntary admission when legal standards are met.
Would repeal DRIPA and replace it with a defined reconciliation framework including landowners, businesses and local governments.
Supports forestry, mining and LNG with environmental standards, predictable permitting timelines, and timely approval decisions.

canwest-party.statusNote: No party website or published positions found.

freedom-party-of-bc.statusNote: No 2026 platform published; positions from the undated 'Our Platform' section of the party's website (checked 2026-10-05).

positions.summary: Calls for lowering taxes across the board, saying lower taxes would ease life for residents and spur industry growth.
Would end foreign ownership of B.C. housing and agricultural land and aims to make housing affordable again.
Pledges support for the natural resource industry and lower taxes to grow industries that create jobs.
Would explore a B.C. provincial police force in place of the RCMP and municipal police, and protect legal firearm owners.
Proposes meeting directly with First Nations chiefs and members to understand what reconciliation means to them.
Supports developing oil, gas, minerals, timber and agriculture, and would investigate authorities' claims about climate change.
